newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Man dies in stampede for Queen's stamp in HK.
newsitem.headline: Man dies in stampede for Queen's stamp in HK.

text.p: A Hong Kong man collapsed and died on Tuesday in a stampede to buy the last stock of Hong Kong stamps to feature British Queen Elizabeth's head.
The man collapsed under the strain of queueing with thousands of stamp fanciers, some of whom had been there all night, to purchase the stamps bearing the British monarch's head, police said.
"There was no sign of life when he arrived at the hospital," a spokesman at Queen Mary Hospital said. The man was not named.

Elizabeth's head is no longer printed on new stamps in the British colony, and those carrying it will cease to be valid on July 1 when the territory is handed back to China after more than 150 years of colonial rule. What was at stake on Tuesday was the remaining stock of the old definitives.
Hong Kong stamps are highly prized by collectors, and stamp fever has swept the territory over the past year as the change of flag looms, making present stamps likely collector's items.
The value of some commemorative stamps grows by up to 20 times within days of their issue.
Last month, collectors queued up a night ahead to buy a series marking the Chinese Lunar Year of the Ox, the last lunar new year stamps to feature an image of the British crown.
Thousands more lined up to buy first issues of colourful new stamps featuring the Hong Kong skyline that are replacing the definitives that bear the queen's head.
